claim: A-CDM is fully implemented at 34 European airports including Amsterdam, Barcelona, Frankfurt, London Heathrow, Paris CDG and Munich.
source_title: Airport collaborative decision-making (A-CDM) impact assessment
supporting_excerpt: A-CDM is fully implemented in 34 airports across Europe, including major hubs such as Amsterdam, Barcelona, Frankfurt, London Heathrow, Paris CDG, and Munich.
caveat: EUROCONTROL is the network manager and thus not fully independent of A-CDM adoption; however, the deployment count is auditable from public airport records.

claim: Average taxi-out time savings from A-CDM range 0.25 to 3 minutes per departure.
source_title: Airport collaborative decision-making (A-CDM) impact assessment
supporting_excerpt: average taxi-out time savings range between 0.25 and 3 minutes per departure.
data_vintage: post-implementation observations across ECAC A-CDM airports
caveat: Range not decomposed by airport in the summary; site-level results vary widely with baseline taxi times and layout.

claim: Wider A-CDM deployment across Europe could reduce total network ATFM delays by 18-23% and improve sector capacity by up to 4%.
source_title: Airport collaborative decision-making (A-CDM) impact assessment
supporting_excerpt: studies show that wider A-CDM deployment across Europe could reduce total network ATFM delays by 18-23% and improve sector capacity by up to 4%.
units: percent reduction in ATFM delays; percent improvement in sector capacity
denominator: total network delays; sector capacity baseline
caveat: Modeled forecast, not measured outcome.

claim: Over 34% of ECAC departures originate from a CDM airport and transmit improved take-off estimates to EUROCONTROL as Network Manager.
source_title: Airport collaborative decision-making (A-CDM) impact assessment
supporting_excerpt: Over 34% of ECAC departures now originate from a CDM airport and transmit improved pre-departure take-off time estimates to EUROCONTROL as the Network Manager.

claim: Munich Airport reports up to 3 minutes taxi-out savings per departure and up to 2 minutes schedule adherence improvement per flight after A-CDM implementation.
source_title: Munich Airport CDM
supporting_excerpt: Average taxi-out time savings of up to 3 minutes per departure ... Average schedule adherence improvements of up to 2 minutes per flight.
units: minutes per departure; minutes per flight
caveat: Airport-reported to a EUROCONTROL workshop; not independently audited, but TTOT accuracy is independently verifiable via network data.

claim: Toronto Pearson reports a 44% reduction in average taxi-in time after deploying Assaia's turnaround-control AI, integrated with the airport's A-CDM initiative.
source_title: 44% Reduction in Average Taxi-In Time achieved at Toronto Pearson International Airport
supporting_excerpt: 44% Reduction in Average Taxi-In Time achieved at Toronto Pearson International Airport.
units: percent reduction in average taxi-in time
caveat: Vendor-published; baseline definition, seasonality, and confounding operational changes not fully disclosed.

claim: Assaia's Turnaround Control has been rolled out across all 106 gates at Toronto Pearson International Airport.
source_title: Toronto Pearson Deploys Assaia's ApronAI to Optimise Operations
supporting_excerpt: Assaia's Turnaround Control technology is being rolled out at the airport's 106 gates.
caveat: Announcement scope; roll-out completion by gate not tracked in this source.

claim: Alaska Airlines reports a 12% reduction in aircraft turn times at Seattle-Tacoma (~4 minutes per departure) and a 17% reduction in excess hold time using Assaia's technology.
source_title: AI aircraft turnarounds cut airport delays by 25% and save millions
supporting_excerpt: Alaska Airlines has reported a 12% reduction in aircraft turn times using Assaia's technology, equating to nearly four minutes saved per departure. Additionally, Assaia's technology contributed to a 17% reduction in excess hold time at the same location.
airport_or_entity: Alaska Airlines at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA)
units: percent reduction in turn time and hold time; minutes per departure
caveat: Traces back to Assaia case-study material; treat as vendor-adjacent even though reported via trade press.

claim: Hong Kong International Airport developed the 'HKIA Digital Twin' in partnership with CHAIN Technology Development, integrating real-time IoT data into a 3D visualization with predictive analytics.
source_title: Digital Twin: A Real-Time Interactive Airport Visualization Tool (ACI World Insights)
supporting_excerpt: The 'HKIA Digital Twin' was developed in partnership between the Airport Authority and CHAIN Technology Development Co. Ltd., which collects real-time data fed from Internet of things (IoT) devices deployed throughout the airport and transforms it into easy-to-read formats. With the use of predictive analytics, it can also provide alerts to the airport community.
caveat: ACI-published summary of an operator initiative; capex and ROI not disclosed.

claim: HKIA formally announced digital twin deployment as part of its smart-airport program in 2019.
source_title: Airport Authority Press Release, HKIA (2019)
supporting_excerpt: Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA) is deploying digital twins as part of its drive to become a smart airport.
caveat: Operator press release; scope and cost not disclosed.

claim: American Airlines launched biometric boarding at DFW in August 2019 (Terminal D international) with planned expansion to approximately 75 international gates across Terminals A, B, C and D by year end.
source_title: Biometric Boarding Arrives at DFW for American Airlines Customers
supporting_excerpt: American customers traveling on select international departures from DFW Terminal D can enjoy additional convenience during the departure process with a one-step facial recognition program ... American planned to expand biometric boarding to nearly 75 international gates throughout Terminals A, B, C and D by the end of 2019.
caveat: Airline press release; actual completion of the 75-gate rollout not verified in this source.

claim: CBP launched Simplified Arrival at DFW, using biometric facial comparison against a gallery from passport/visa photos to automate manual document checks.
source_title: CBP's Simplified Arrival Lands at DFW
supporting_excerpt: Simplified Arrival uses facial recognition to match a traveler's face to an image already submitted to CBP, typically from a passport or visa photo, with a live comparison photo taken when the traveler arrives at a DFW inspection point.
airport_or_entity: US Customs and Border Protection at DFW

claim: SITA reports its Smart Path biometric single-token product is in use at 45 airports worldwide including Beijing (PEK), Bangkok (BKK) and Newark (EWR).
source_title: SITA Smart Path biometrics launched for domestic US passengers as airport investments accelerate (Biometric Update)
supporting_excerpt: SITA's biometrics systems are currently in use at 45 airports worldwide, including major hubs like Beijing (PEK), Bangkok (BKK) and Newark (EWR).
caveat: Vendor-reported figure carried via trade press; deployment scope per airport not detailed.

claim: Xovis supplies queue length and waiting time measurements at 10-minute intervals across airport facilities using overhead 3D computer-vision sensors.
source_title: Airport software (Xovis)
supporting_excerpt: XOVIS supplies facility-level measurements of queue length and waiting time at 10-minute intervals across terminal facilities, using computer vision sensors to continuously estimate congestion states.
caveat: Vendor documentation; independent audit of accuracy not cited here.

claim: Amadeus AODB is cloud-hosted and holds schedules for 95% of airlines one year in advance.
source_title: Amadeus Airport Operational Data Base (AODB)
supporting_excerpt: AODB holds schedules for 95% of airlines 1 year in advance ... Amadeus Airport Operational Data Base (AODB) is cloud-hosted.
caveat: Vendor documentation; deployment cost not disclosed publicly.

claim: Heathrow Terminal 5's opening in 2008 misplaced approximately 42,000 bags in the first days of operation and led to significant BA flight cancellations, on a £4.3 billion terminal.
source_title: Thousands of Bags Miss Flights at British Airways Heathrow Terminal 5, Again (IEEE Spectrum)
supporting_excerpt: The failure of the baggage handling system, which was not fully tested before the terminal's opening, resulted in over 42,000 bags being misplaced in the first few days of operation.
caveat: Bag count varies across sources (28,000 to 42,000+); £4.3B figure is the widely reported nominal terminal capex.

claim: Heathrow T5's chaotic opening was directly attributable to poor BAA/BA cooperation, inadequate staff training, and late testing of the baggage system.
source_title: T5: The lessons learned (Business Traveller)
supporting_excerpt: The chaotic opening on March 27 of the £4.3 billion terminal was a result of poor communication and preparation on the part of both BAA and British Airways ... TSC also cited poor staff training and system testing by BA as significantly contributory.
caveat: Contemporary trade-press synthesis of parliamentary Transport Select Committee findings.

claim: Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER) was delayed nearly a decade with costs ballooning to approximately €6 billion from an initial €2 billion budget; a bespoke fire-safety control system that could not be correctly programmed was a central driver of the delay.
source_title: Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER): A €10 Billion Disaster Of Delays And Corruption
supporting_excerpt: The automatic fire extinguishing system designed specifically for BER was non-functional because no one could program it correctly. During the construction phase, fire doors, cabling and sprinklers had faults, and costs ballooned to €6 billion from an initial budget of €2 billion.
caveat: Total lifetime cost figures for BER vary across sources; €10B is a commonly cited all-in estimate. €6B and €2B figures are as reported in the cited source.

claim: In 2025 Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER) suffered a cyberattack via an external check-in and baggage-handling vendor, causing manual check-ins, baggage delays, and flight delays.
source_title: Cyber-attack disruption continues at BER (International Airport Review)
supporting_excerpt: Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER) has been hit by a significant cyberattack that targeted the external provider responsible for the airport's computer-controlled passenger and baggage handling system, resulting in severe operational disruptions.
caveat: Trade-press synthesis; vendor identity and technical vector not fully public.

claim: American Airlines' new Admirals Club near the Terminal C Skylink station is approximately 37,000 square feet and described by American as its largest Admirals Club to date; a scaled-down 'Provisions by Admirals Club' grab-and-go concept is planned for Terminal F.
source_title: Airport Context Packet - DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: Admirals Club (new, Terminal C): Approximately 37,000 square feet near the Skylink station - described by American as its largest Admirals Club to date. Terminal F lounge posture (as announced): A Provisions by Admirals Club grab-and-go concept - a scaled-down offering rather than a Flagship-tier lounge - is planned for Terminal F.
airport_or_entity: American Airlines at DFW Terminal C and Terminal F
caveat: Context packet synthesizes public American Airlines announcements and DFW newsroom material; source packet flags the Terminal F lounge posture as a live signal, not a settled decision.

claim: Terminal F is scoped at 31 gates, approximately $4 billion, with American Airlines as sole occupant; first phase operational in 2027 and full program targeted for 2030; the Use and Lease Agreement extends through 2043.

supporting_excerpt: DFW and American announced acceleration and expansion of Terminal F to 31 gates at approximately $4 billion, with the Use and Lease Agreement extended through 2043. American is the sole occupant of Terminal F. First phase scheduled to be operational in 2027; full program targeted for 2030.
caveat: Context packet synthesizes DFW and American public announcements; specific gate mix and internal square footage not public.

claim: Terminal F is being built using a modular method with gates built offsite and installed on site, with reported approximately 30 percent cost savings versus conventional construction; the same modular method is being applied to Terminal C and Terminal A renovations, adding 14 gates by spring 2026.
source_title: Airport Context Packet - DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: Modular. Gates are being built offsite and installed on site. DFW and secondary sources report approximately 30% cost savings versus conventional construction. The same modular method is being applied to Terminal C and Terminal A renovations, which are adding 14 gates by spring 2026.
caveat: 30% savings figure originates in DFW-adjacent communications; independent audit not cited in the context packet.

claim: Bentley markets an airport digital twin product line whose case studies are predominantly asset-management applications integrated with reality modeling and BIM.
source_title: Digital Twins for Airport Operations and Expansion (Bentley)
supporting_excerpt: Digital Twins for Airport Operations and Expansion (Bentley product landing page describing airport digital twin use cases spanning asset management, expansion and operations).

source_title: Solutions (Amorph.aero)
